All atoms are assigned. A bound on each sign allows extension through syntax; agreement on every atom gives uniqueness.
The Boolean truth fiber extends the two signed axioms and is complete and consistent. In the other direction, pull back the two complementary subobjects along the atom morphism.
In every consistent extension of an admitting target the theorem and refutation domains are inseparable. Smullyan supplies historical comparison with strong separation.
The primitive-recursive numeral-instance function is fixed. A recursive proposed sentence separator has a recursive inverse image and the two domain inclusions have their specified orientation.

The choose-second-on-membership conditional is total in the standard model. A numerical program index supplies a partial syntactic morphism with exactly that value. The domain comparison excludes the lift.

For every fixed representation its first-digit decision separates the cuts. The proof that a fixed set cannot have a single uniform deciding program uses source inseparability and the complementary partial identities of a uniform decision.
For the fork the ordinary relative computation comparison fails already for restriction equivalence by the number of restriction idempotents on a terminal object.

At each vertex the two c.e. subsets include every element of that carrier and are disjoint. Their tagged coproduct is invertible there. Naturality for both transitions holds for the component inverses. This yields a total decision on the diagram.

Fix an endpoint, a set of c.e. axioms in that language and a consistent deductive closure extending the endpoint theory. The union of positive and negative atom codes cannot cover; an actual omitted index is obtained.
Postcomposition along the inclusion is a fully faithful restriction functor. Both its adjunctions use ordinary hom-set equivalences with the reindexing functor.

For arbitrary finite spectra C, the two signed size-sentence code functions are computable. The canonical model satisfies precisely the indexed size choices. For recursive C the signed axioms have c.e. codes. Full-model theorem words and deductive-closure theorem words are compared separately with C in the supplemental checks.
Corollary 4.8 gives the internal characterization. The printed comparison assumes equivalence of the two separator-existence predicates and combines the two iff statements.
Each structured-arrow object has exactly one arrow out of the free object. Its underlying map is obtained by extending the given assignment and the adjunction unit is the atom map.
The generated closed theory is a lower bound of all closed theories containing those axioms. It itself belongs to this family, which proves that it is their greatest lower bound.

The signed arithmetic pair is a specific witness. Finite supports taken from both proof trees give one valuation into the given PA model. Both truth judgements hold with that same valuation, contradicting opposite conclusions.
